name: Chibcha

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Chibcha (chib1270).

notes: Chibchan language (Muisca) of the Colombian highlands, extinct since the late 18th century. There is no living pronunciation; phonemic values are RECONSTRUCTED from the colonial Spanish-based orthography of de Lugo (1619) and later grammars, following Constenla (1984) and Gonzalez de Perez (2006). Every value is tentative: c and qu both spell /k/, and the sibilant/affricate series z/ch/x (here read as retroflex) is the chief point of dispute. The grapheme y (an inverse-ypsilon in the sources) denotes the high central vowel. Stress, vowel length and nasalization are not recovered from the spelling. STRESS EXEMPTION (documented): the language is extinct with no living pronunciation to derive word-stress placement from, and none of the read reconstructions (Constenla 1984; Gonzalez de Perez 2006) recovers it from the colonial spelling -- no `stress` block is added. RESEARCH: citation-verified 2026-08 (sources wave 4) -- Constenla (1984, 'Los fonemas del muisca', Estudios de Linguistica Chibcha 2:65-111) and Gonzalez de Perez (2006, 'Aproximacion al sistema fonetico-fonologico de la lengua muisca', Instituto Caro y Cuervo) are now formally listed in `sources` (previously named only in prose); both are real, independently-published comparative reconstructions, and the two disagreeing on some sibilant/affricate values is exactly why this spec keeps those values flagged tentative rather than picking one silently. Gold: wikipron (n=99, PER 0.13; see benchmarks/results.json).
